newsitem.title: USA: Calif. controller to repay $1.36 bln to Calpers.
newsitem.headline: Calif. controller to repay $1.36 bln to Calpers.

text.p: California's controller agreed on Wednesday to immediately repay the state's largest pension fund $1.36 billion, money lawmakers improperly used to balance state budgets in the early 1990s.

In a statement, state Controller Kathleen Connell said she would repay the California Public Employees' Retirement System (Calpers) once the state Department of Finance certifies that California's treasury has the needed funds.
On Tuesday, Gov. Pete Wilson ordered the state to immediately make the Calpers payment.
The state's Republican governor said by repaying the entire amount during the 1997-1998 fiscal year, California taxpayers would save at least $650 million in interest.

State lawmakers had hoped to pay the money back over several years. But Calpers was "unwilling to offer an affordable" repayment plan, forcing the state to pay the money back in a lump sum out of its 1997-1998 budget, Wilson said.
With more than $100 billion in assets, Calpers is the largest public pension system in the United States.
Calpers manages retirement and health plans serving more than one million workers, retirees and their families.

A state appeals court ruled in February that the governor and the legislature improperly withheld the money from Calpers in the early 1990s to balance state budgets during California's deepest economic downturn since the Depression. In May, the state Supreme Court refused to rehear the case.

Wilson said repaying Calpers $1.36 billion this year would require lawmakers to sharply curtail their spending plans. Funding for Wilson's tax cut proposals and money for other non-education programs could be eliminated, the governor said.
Controller Connell said paying Calpers back immediately would "assure that state retirees are no longer political chips in a partisan budget debate."
She said repayment "provides an avenue for ending an exhaustive and expensive budget stalemate."
California lawmakers have yet to approve the state's budget for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1. The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
